Index: lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-qt/status.md
===================================================================
--- lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-qt/status.md	
+++ lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-qt/status.md	
@@ -1,329 +1,336 @@
 # pathland-render-qt — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** October 20, 2026
 
 The **Qt Quick renderer**: maps opcode frames incrementally onto a Qt Quick
 scene graph (shared-memory desktop path). Protocol contract: `spec/`.
 Design-token contract: `spec/TOKENS.md`.
 
 **Language split.** The crate is a **hybrid**:
 - **Rust** owns the shared decode core (`pathland-render-core`), a sent-state
   **delta diff** that turns each frame into a batch of C-compatible commands,
   the `Pump` transport seam (frames in / events out), the Qt main-loop shell,
   and the C ABI for foreign hosts.
 - **C++** (in `src/qt/`) owns the Qt application shell (QGuiApplication +
   QQuickWindow + QQmlEngine + a QML-facing `Bridge` QObject) and applies the
   delta command batch to QML items. Built via `cc` + `moc` in `build.rs`;
   needs Qt6 dev libs (Homebrew: `qtbase qtdeclarative qtmultimedia`).
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Build/toolchain**: `build.rs` locates Qt via `qmake -query` (Homebrew +
   Linux CI), runs `moc` on the bridge, compiles the C++ layer with `cc`, and
   links the Qt frameworks/dylibs (framework search via the transitive
   `rustc-link-search=framework` kind, so demo binaries link too). The protocol
   core (`pathland-core`/`view`) stays `no_std`/wasm-safe.
 - **FFI boundary** (`src/ffi.rs` + `src/qt/pathland_qt.h`): a flat
   `PathlandQtCommand` batch (create/delete/insert/remove/move/set-text/
   set-property/set-string-property/reset-node/set-scheme) plus a
   `PathlandQtEvent` (pointer-up/value-changed/text-changed) flowing C++ → Rust.
 - **Delta diff** (`src/renderer.rs`): `QtRenderer` keeps a sent-state cache and
   emits only the commands that change it — an unchanged tree emits **zero**
   commands. Property changes re-send the node's *complete* property set
   preceded by `RESET_NODE` (so the C++ layer resets removed properties to
   renderer defaults). Numeric props are emitted with `VALUE` last (Qt Quick
   clamps a control's value when `from`/`to` aren't configured yet). Tree roots
   are children of pseudo-parent `0` (window contentItem). Ghost children after
   `DELETE_NODE` are guarded in the walk. Headless-tested.
 - **Qt widget mapping** (`src/qt/qt_layer.cpp`): component → QML item factory —
   `VSTACK`/`HSTACK`/lazy stacks → a **wrapper `Item` holding an inner
   `ColumnLayout`/`RowLayout`** (`QtQuick.Layouts`; the wrapper's `plPad` drives
   padding + implicit size, so a stack hugs its content), `GRID`+lazy grids →
   `Grid`, `ZSTACK` → `Item` (children share one box, positioned by the 2D
   `ALIGNMENT` code on both axes, re-derived on resize; the Hug stack's own size
   is the **max child** per axis, and an "effectively FILL" child — explicit
   `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT=FILL`, a greedy primitive, or fill propagation through a
   nested stack/Spacers — stretches to the box), `SCROLLVIEW` → `ScrollView`
   (content attaches to its
   `contentItem`; fills its parent by default), `TEXT` → `Text`, `SPACER`/
   unknown → `Item`, `DIVIDER` → `Rectangle`, `COLOR` → `Rectangle`, `SHAPE` →
   `Rectangle` with `SHAPE_KIND` geometry (Circle/Capsule/Ellipse round to
   `min(w,h)/2` — Ellipse is a uniform-radius approximation; Rectangle is
   square-cornered; RoundedRectangle keeps `BORDER_RADIUS`; `Path` unsupported),
   `IMAGE` → `Image`, `BUTTON` → `Button`, `TEXT_FIELD` → `TextField`, `SLIDER`
   → `Slider`, `TOGGLE` → `Switch` (controls embed `onX: bridge.<event>(id, …)`
   handlers), `PROGRESS_VIEW`/`GAUGE` → `ProgressBar` (fraction via `PROGRESS`,
   activity via `IS_INDETERMINATE`), `STEPPER` → `SpinBox`, `PICKER` → `ComboBox`
   (option children populate the model ordered by insertion; `SELECTION` →
   `currentIndex`; `onActivated` → `VALUE_CHANGED`), `MENU` → `Button` trigger
   (Qt 6 has no MenuButton; a popup Menu is a documented gap), `DATE_PICKER` /
   `COLOR_PICKER` → `TextField`/`Button` approximations (Qt Quick Controls has no
   native date/color pickers). Property application via generic `setProperty`
   (Qt ignores unknown props): spacing/`align`/padding+edges, width/height (`-1`
   FILL → **`Layout.fillWidth`/`fillHeight` in a layout, anchors.fill elsewhere**,
   `-2` HUG → implicit), color, **font size/weight/family/style via the `font`
   `QFont` property** (dotted-path `setProperty` silently fails), opacity, visible,
   z, value/min/max/step, selected→checked, enabled,
   `IS_SECURE` → `echoMode` = `TextInput.Password` (masked), progress/indeterminate,
   selection→currentIndex, prompt/label→placeholder, image source.
   **`OFFSET_X`/`OFFSET_Y`** are a post-layout QML `Translate` transform (composes
   with layout/alignment instead of being overwritten). **`ALLOWS_HIT_TESTING`**
   disables the item's mouse acceptance and any attached pointer MouseArea without
   hiding it. **Stack alignment**: a stack's `ALIGNMENT` positions each child on
   the cross axis via
   its `Layout` attached properties (Start/Center/End; `Fill`(3)/absent = default
   HUG/start, never a stretch — spec/LAYOUT.md).
   **Roots are anchored to fill the window** (GTK hexpand/vexpand parity).
   `RESET_NODE` resets renderer-owned style defaults (value props untouched so a
   slider/toggle doesn't lose position on echo).
 - **Diff ordering** (`src/renderer.rs`): `QtRenderer::diff` emits child inserts
   *before* property deltas, so `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`/`ALIGNMENT` land after a widget is
   attached to its final parent — FILL resolves against the real parent instead of
   the create-time contentItem placeholder.
 - **Events** (spec/EVENTS.md guards): the `Bridge` reports control inputs
   (`tap` → `POINTER_UP`, `valueChanged` → `VALUE_CHANGED`, `textChanged` →
   `TEXT_CHANGED`) to Rust, which encodes the `Event`, writes it into the event
   ring, and wakes the host (renderer never drains). Interactions are gated by
   `BINDING_ID`/`ACTION_ID` and programmatic value sets suppress echoes.
 - **Pointer event streams**: an `EVENT_LISTENERS`-gated QML `MouseArea` overlay
   is attached to any node carrying pointer listener bits (down/move/up), and
   its handlers report `POINTER_DOWN`/`POINTER_MOVE`/`POINTER_UP` through the
   Bridge (bypassing the `BINDING_ID` gate — any element can emit raw inputs,
   spec/EVENTS.md). Attached/detached on listener-mask changes / `RESET` /
   `DELETE`.
 - **Native back / `NAVIGATE`**: a window-level `KeyFilter` maps Escape to
   `Event::Navigate { url: None }` (global, never node-keyed), matching the GTK
   renderer. BackSpace is deferred (needs text-focus detection).
 - **Color-scheme detection (spec/TOKENS.md)**: `QStyleHints::colorSchemeChanged`
   fires a scheme event to Rust, which calls `QtRenderer::set_scheme` — the
   shared core re-resolves design tokens and the diff re-emits the changed
   concrete values (`SET_PROPERTY`) with no host wake. Initial scheme applied at
   init.
 - **`META::RESET`**: both pump paths scan each frame for `META::RESET` and call
   `QtRenderer::reset()` (clears the decoded tree, sent-state cache, and the
   C++ scene incl. listener overlays).
 - **Qt shell**: init/run split (headless tests drive `init` + `apply` without
   an event loop); `pathland_qt_layer_run` owns the window + a zero-millisecond
   idle `QTimer` that ticks Rust's pump (Qt analogue of GTK's idle pump).
 - **Asset root** (`pathland_qt_set_asset_root` /
   `pathland_qt_layer_set_asset_root`): web-style `/_pathland/...` image/media
   sources resolve against a host-extracted local directory (the Qt analogue of
   `pathland_gtk_set_asset_root`); the Java Qt host extracts `DemoAssets` and
   sets it before `runRing`.
 - **C ABI for foreign hosts** (`src/capi.rs`): `pathland_qt_run(host,
   on_event)` (over a `pathland-view-native` `NativeHost`) and
   `pathland_qt_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)` (over a borrowed
   `libpathland_core` ring), both mirroring the GTK renderer's contract. Passes
   a bare program name to Qt.
 - **Rust demo ergonomics** (`run`): `pathland_qt::run(app_id, title,
   Rc<RefCell<RingTransport>>, on_event)` mirrors `pathland_render_gtk::run`;
   the pump borrow is held across frame application (zero-copy batch view of the
   shared ring).
 
 - **Navigation adapter (spec DSL.md §4.5)**: a VSTACK/HSTACK slot carrying the
   `ROUTE` property promotes to the renderer's nav container and reconciles a
   page stack **by depth** (`NAV_DEPTH`): pop down to the app's depth, then
   `Refresh` (same route), `Push` (deeper + new route), or `Replace` (same
   depth, new route) — mirroring the GTK `AdwNavigationView` adapter. `PlatformDefault`
   chrome wraps each page in a header with a native back button (`→`
   `navigateBack` → `Event::Navigate { url: None }`); `NAV_CHROME=1` (`Custom`)
   pushes the bare destination. The back-stack stays app-owned; the page stack
   is the renderer's rendered-output cache. **Implementation note:** Qt Quick
   has no native navigation container and `StackView`'s `push`/`pop` are
   QML-callable-only (not invokable from C++ via `QMetaObject`), so the nav
   container is a plain `Item` whose pages the renderer manages (only the top
   visible) — a renderer-owned page cache, same statelessness contract.
   **Page sizing:** each page wrapper is anchored to fill the nav container
   (`placeDestination`), so the header/content/destination chain is sized and the
   destination subtree fills the content area (previously the page wrapper was
   attached unsized, collapsing the content to 0×0 and showing only an
   overflowing title).
 
 - **Post-merge protocol parity (October 2026)**: the crate was merged onto the
   shared `PARAMETER` rename and now maps the protocol surface added on `main`:
   - `ICON` (0x0B) → a `Text` item whose glyph is resolved from `ICON_NAME` by a
     renderer-owned canonical-name map (unknown names fall back to a dot), with
     `COLOR`/`FONT_SIZE` reuse (spec/ICONS.md).
   - `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` (0x30) → **non-visual** (layout-transparent: created but
     never attached) hosting a QML `MediaPlayer` + `AudioOutput`
     (spec/MEDIA.md).
   - `VIDEO` (0x0A) → a `VideoOutput` surface; `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID` binds its
     `source` to the referenced controller's `MediaPlayer` (a reference, not a
     parent/child edge).
   - `PROXY_VIEW` (0x1E) → a transparent vertical container.
   - `SIZE_THAT_FITS` (0x17) → a greedy two-axis slot; its one selected child
     fills it.
   - `GRID_ROW` (0x1D) → a row-grouping container whose cells flatten into
     the parent Grid.
 - **Shared decode parity** (`pathland-render-core`): `LIST`-typed properties
   (`FIT_QUERY`) decode into `HostNode::lists`, and `PARAMETER::SET_DATE` into
   `HostNode::date` — so the Qt layer can measure fit slots and format dates.
 - **`SIZE_THAT_FITS` fit measurement**: the slot's `FIT_QUERY` thresholds reach
   the C++ layer as CSV; a width change derives the fit index (largest
   `minWidth` ≤ allocated width; equal thresholds keep the lower index; empty
   table → 0) and reports `FIT_CHANGED` once after the first measure, then only
   when the index changes. The report is a layout result, not a value echo, so
   it is not suppressed while a frame's properties are applied. The slot shows
   exactly one selected child, which fills the slot.
 - **`GRID_ROW` flattening**: a row's cells attach directly to the parent Grid
   (row-major), so columns align across rows; the row item takes no cell.
 - **`DATE_PICKER`**: `SET_DATE` (days since epoch + millis of day) renders as an
   ISO date (with time when nonzero) in a QML text field — a QML approximation
   (Qt Quick has no native date picker).
 - **Events** (spec/EVENTS.md): pointer `hover`/`leave` (`POINTER_MOVE`
   hovering/leaving) from the listener `MouseArea`; `KEY_DOWN`/`KEY_UP` for the
   focused text input (component-type/key-listener gated); `FOCUS_CHANGED` /
   `EDITING_CHANGED` / `SUBMIT` for text inputs (gated by the matching
   `EVENT_LISTENERS` bits); BackSpace is native back unless a text input is
   focused (focus-aware, no longer deferred).
 - **Visual styling layer** (parity with the web/GTK demos):
   - `BACKGROUND_COLOR` / `BORDER_*` / `BORDER_RADIUS` render on a background
     `Rectangle` behind a container's content (stacks reuse an injected
     `pl<id>bg`; plain containers create one lazily); `Rectangle`-backed nodes
     set them directly. `RESET_NODE` clears them.
   - **Composite control mode** (spec/PRIMITIVES.md §2): a `Button` that gains
     children is promoted from the native widget to a bare `Item`+`ColumnLayout`
     shell that renders the app's `ButtonStyle` body, so `PlainButtonStyle` /
     `BorderedButtonStyle` buttons look like the web/GTK ones. Leaf buttons stay
     native.
   - **Foreground inheritance** (CSS `color`): a container's `COLOR` is inherited
     by descendant `Text`/`Icon` that don't set their own.
   - **Layout defaults (spec/LAYOUT.md)**: the cross axis **hugs** by default
     (never CSS `align-items:stretch`); only an *effectively FILL* child stretches
     — explicit `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT=FILL`, a layout-greedy primitive (`SPACER` main,
     `DIVIDER` cross, `COLOR`/`SCROLLVIEW`/`SIZE_THAT_FITS` both), or **fill
     propagation** (a Hug stack/ZStack/proxy whose subtree carries a FILL
     child/greedy filler). `ALIGNMENT` only positions (`Fill(3)` = default hug).
     Recomputed at each frame boundary (`recomputeLayout`), so `RESET_NODE`'s
     style reset can't wipe it. Plus `CONTENT_MARGINS`.
   - **`TEXT_STYLE`** applies a base typography (size + weight) that raw
     `FONT_SIZE`/`FONT_WEIGHT` override; **`SHADOW_*`** draws a best-effort
     offset shadow layer.
 - **Media transport** (spec/MEDIA.md): `MEDIA_SOURCE`, `PLAYBACK_STATE`
   (play/pause), `MEDIA_POSITION` (seek, seconds→ms), `MEDIA_VOLUME` /
   `MEDIA_MUTED` (via `AudioOutput`), `MEDIA_LOOP`, `MEDIA_RATE`, and the
   `MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED` / `MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED` / `MEDIA_ENDED` /
   `MEDIA_VOLUME_CHANGED` / `MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED` reports (reported by the
   controller's component type, not gated by `BINDING_ID`; programmatic sets are
   echo-suppressed). A play/pause declared before the source is re-applied when
   the source lands.
 - **Layout/property parity**: `OFFSET_X/Y`, `POSITION_X/Y`, `MIN/IDEAL/MAX_*`,
   `CONTENT_MODE` (image fit/fill), `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`, `BORDER_COLOR` /
   `BORDER_WIDTH` / `BORDER_RADIUS`, `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`, `LINE_LIMIT`,
   `TRUNCATION_MODE`, and `GRID_COLUMNS` (via the `Layout` attached properties
   where applicable).
 - **Headless test hang fixed**: Qt adds the executable's directory to QML's
   implicit import path; a `cargo test` binary lives in a huge `target/debug/deps`
   and plugin resolution scanned it for minutes. The shell now drops the
   application directory from the engine's import path at init, so
   `cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` completes in ~2s (no copy-to-temp workaround).
 
 ## Not implemented / gaps
 
 - **`MENU` popup item list**: Qt 6 has no `MenuButton`; the trigger is a
   `Button` and the action-item popup is not built (documented gap).
 - **`COLOR_PICKER`** remains a `Button` approximation (a QML color-swatch popup
   is a follow-up); `DATE_PICKER` is an ISO-text QML approximation, not a native
   dialog.
 - **`PICKER` option styling** and `SHAPE` path approximation. Native **leaf**
   controls keep Qt Quick Controls' own chrome (background/border); the styling
   layer covers containers, composite controls, and `Rectangle`-backed nodes.
 - **Icons** are renderer-owned glyphs (the canonical `ICON_NAME` → a Unicode
   symbol), not the web's SVG/Lucide set — recognizable but not pixel-identical.
 - **Shadows** are an offset rectangle approximation, not a blurred
   `MultiEffect` shadow.
 - **Keys/events beyond the focused text input**: keys are reported for a focused
   text input; keys on other focused controls, `SCROLL`/`WHEEL`, and
   `DATE_CHANGED` are not yet reported. Hover/leave use `POINTER_MOVE` (the
   listener mask bit).
 - **FILL inside plain positioners**: `GRID` (a `QQuickGrid`) rejects
   `anchors.fill` on its children, so a `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` `FILL` inside a Grid
   defers and is skipped (the positioner sizes it). Stacks use `RowLayout`/
   `ColumnLayout` so FILL children stretch properly.
 - The Rust DSL does not yet expose signal property bindings (the Java DSL
   does), so the demo marks the slider bound via a `BINDING_ID` on the retained
   tree; a real `.value(Signal)` DSL binding is a DSL/engine feature.
 - The Rust DSL has no `NavigationContainer` (the spec table is aspirational) —
   the renderer consumes ROUTE/NAV_DEPTH (exercised by the nav adapter tests).
 - `TRANSITION`-hint animation, back-swipe gestures, multi-step deep-link
   intermediate pages (same gaps as the GTK renderer).
 - **Java JNA demo** (`lib/java/pathland-qt-demo`) runs the shared
   `MusicPlayerView` (app-driven media) via `pathland_qt_run_ring`.
 - Lazy views render eagerly.

Now I have a complete understanding of the padding implementation. Let me analyze it for spec alignment and completeness.

**Spec for padding (MODIFIERS.md):**
- `.padding(_:)` → `PADDING` 0x1011 (uniform, one SET_PROPERTY)
- `.padding(edges:)` / `.padding(_:edges:)` → per-edge `PADDING_TOP/RIGHT/BOTTOM/LEFT`
- Semantics: "PADDING is uniform and shorthand; a per-edge modifier overwrites the edge only. Per-edge wins over uniform when both are present."
- "Any modifier applies to any view (`.padding` works on a `Text` and a `VStack` alike)." — So padding should work on a Text too, not just stacks!

**Current implementation:**
1. `applyPadding(item, edge, value)`:
   - `lay = layoutOf(item)` → for a stack wrapper, returns the inner layout; for a non-stack (e.g., Text), returns nullptr → returns early (no-op).
   - So padding only works on stacks (VStack/HStack/lazy/proxy) and composite controls (which have a layout wrapper). It does NOT work on Text/Image/etc. — which is a spec deviation ("padding works on a Text and a VStack alike").
   - For uniform: sets `plPad` (drives implicit size + anchors.margins) and `anchors.margins = value`.
   - For per-edge: sets `anchors.topMargin/rightMargin/bottomMargin/leftMargin`. Note: per-edge does NOT update `plPad`/implicit size. So per-edge padding insets the layout but the wrapper's implicit size (hug) does NOT account for it! That's a bug: `implicitWidth = lay.implicitWidth + 2*plPad` only uses `plPad` (uniform), not per-edge margins. So a stack with only per-edge padding hugs incorrectly (ignores the padding in its implicit size).

2. `CONTENT_MARGINS` is treated identically to `PADDING` (uniform). That's a reasonable mapping (spec: CONTENT_MARGINS as an inset), though CONTENT_MARGINS is a separate concept (stack content margins). Probably fine.

3. The `PL_PROP_PADDING_*` per-edge cases map to "topMargin"/"rightMargin"/"bottomMargin"/"leftMargin" on the layout's anchors. These are valid QQuickAnchors properties (margins). Good.

**Gaps/bugs identified:**
1. **Padding on non-stack views** (Text, Image, etc.) is a no-op — spec says padding applies to any view. Need to decide: implement padding on arbitrary views, or document as a gap. This is a real spec deviation.

2. **Per-edge padding doesn't affect the wrapper's implicit size** (hug). Only `plPad` (uniform) is in the implicit-size binding. So `padding(p -> p.top(10))` insets the content but the stack hugs as if no padding (implicit height ignores the 10 top). Actually wait — the layout's `anchors.margins` is set, but `anchors.topMargin` overrides just top. The `implicitHeight: lay.implicitHeight + 2*plPad` uses `plPad` which is 0 for per-edge only. So the wrapper's implicit height = lay.implicitHeight (no padding), while the layout is inset by the per-edge margin. Result: the layout's content + margins may overflow the wrapper's implicit size. This is a bug for per-edge padding + hug sizing.

3. **Per-edge overwrites uniform** — the spec says "per-edge wins over uniform". In the current impl: uniform sets `anchors.margins` and `plPad`; per-edge sets `anchors.topMargin` (which overrides `margins` for that edge). So visually per-edge wins (correct). But `plPad` (used for implicit size) still holds the uniform value, so the implicit size is wrong after per-edge overrides (it still adds 2*plPad even if that edge was overridden). Minor edge case.

So the padding modifier IS implemented for stacks (uniform + per-edge insets the layout), and tested (padding_insets_the_stack_content tests uniform margins + one per-edge topMargin). But there are gaps:

- **Not implemented on non-stack views** (spec: "padding works on a Text and a VStack alike").
- **Per-edge padding not reflected in own-size hug** (implicit size binding only uses uniform `plPad`).

The user asks "What about padding modifier? Is that implemented?" — I should answer: yes, partially implemented for stacks (uniform + per-edge inset), with a test. But list the gaps: (a) non-stack views, (b) per-edge padding's effect on hug implicit size, and (c) the uniform-vs-per-edge precedence nuance.

Let me verify the per-edge own-size claim by checking the implicit size binding again: `implicitHeight: lay ? lay.implicitHeight + 2 * plPad : 0`. Only `plPad`. Per-edge sets `anchors.topMargin` etc., not `plPad`. So yes, per-edge padding isn't in the implicit size.

Also, is there any test for the visual inset of per-edge (child position shifted)? The existing `padding_insets_the_stack_content` only checks the layout's `margins`/`topMargin` property value, not that the child actually moves. And it doesn't check own-size with per-edge.

Let me also verify the "padding on Text" claim — is there a general `PADDING` handling for non-layout items? `applyPadding` early-returns if `!lay`. So no. And there's no other path (e.g., ensureBackground). So padding on Text/Image/Button (non-composite) is a no-op.

Now, should I also check whether the demo uses per-edge padding? Yes: `padding(p -> p.edges(6,12,6,12))` (subtitlePill) and `padding(p -> p.edges(0,0,0,10))` (Divider in LibraryView/NowPlayingSidebar) and `padding(24)` (LibraryView). So per-edge IS used by the demo. The subtitlePill uses `edges(6,12,6,12)` = top 6, right 12, bottom 6, left 12. That's a VStack (subtitlePill). So per-edge padding on a VStack is exercised. But its own-size hug (implicit) would be wrong (ignores the 6/12).

Actually, the subtitlePill VStack has an `offset` and `background`, no explicit frame → hugs. Its implicit size should include the padding. With per-edge padding not in implicit size, the pill's box would be too small (content + only plPad=0). This could actually be a visible bug in the demo (the pill's background rectangle uses `anchors.fill: parent`, so the background would hug the content without padding → the padding is lost visually!).

Wait — actually, how does the background get its size? The pill VStack wrapper has a background Rectangle (`anchors.fill: parent`). The wrapper's size = implicit (hug) or set. The `plPad` drives both `anchors.margins` (content inset) AND implicit size. For per-edge padding, `anchors.margins` isn't set (only per-edge topMargin etc.), and `plPad` stays 0. So:
- The layout (ColumnLayout) is `anchors.fill: parent` with `anchors.margins: plPad = 0`, plus per-edge `topMargin=6, rightMargin=12, bottomMargin=6, leftMargin=12`. So the layout IS inset by 6/12/6/12 (per-edge overrides the 0 margins).
- But the wrapper's implicit size = lay.implicitWidth + 2*0 = lay.implicitWidth (the layout's own implicit size, which is the content size). So the wrapper hugs to the content size WITHOUT the padding. The layout is then inset within a wrapper that's the same size as the content → the content overflows (layout inset 6/12 but wrapper = content size, so content gets clipped/squished or the layout is smaller than content).

Actually, anchors.margins on the layout with anchors.fill means the layout occupies parent minus margins. If the parent (wrapper) is content-sized and the layout is inset, the layout's available width = content width - 12 - 12 = negative/small → content overflows or the layout can't fit.

So per-edge padding on a hug stack is broken. This is a real bug affecting the demo's subtitlePill and the dividers.

So the answer to "is padding implemented?": Yes for uniform on stacks (and tested), but per-edge padding has bugs:
1. Per-edge not reflected in the stack's own-size hug (implicit size).
2. Padding not implemented on non-stack views (spec says it should apply to any view).
3. (minor) uniform-vs-per-edge precedence for implicit size.

Let me also double check: is there a `plPad`-driven implicit size for the background too? The background `Rectangle { anchors.fill: parent }` fills the wrapper regardless. So if the wrapper is too small, the background is too small.

Let me be precise and concise. Let me also verify: does `layoutOf` return the layout for a composite button (which is a wrapper with a ColumnLayout)? Yes (composite uses the same wrapper). So padding works on composite controls too (which is good, since ButtonStyle padding is common).

Let me also check: does padding work on a ScrollView? `applyPadding` requires `layoutOf(item)`; a ScrollView is not a layout → no-op. But ScrollView padding is a spec property ("PADDING/CONTENT_MARGINS as an inset"). So ScrollView padding also no-op. Minor.

Let me write the findings and a plan.

Actually, let me also verify the `CONTENT_MARGINS` handling: it's treated as uniform padding (same as PADDING). CONTENT_MARGINS is a "content margins" property (0x0005). Mapping it to the layout margins (padding) is a reasonable approximation but CONTENT_MARGINS semantics differ (it's the stack's content-area inset). For now it's aliased to padding. Fine to note.

Let me also confirm the per-edge property order/precedence. In the diff, properties are emitted in some order; if both PADDING (uniform) and PADDING_TOP are present, uniform sets margins + plPad, then PADDING_TOP sets topMargin. The order in the BTreeMap: property ids PADDING=0x1011 < PADDING_TOP=0x1012 < RIGHT=0x1013 < BOTTOM=0x1014 < LEFT=0x1015. So uniform first, then per-edge. So per-edge wins on the actual anchors (topMargin overrides margins). Good for the inset. But plPad still uniform → implicit size wrong when edges overridden.

Now let me formulate a clear answer + plan.

Plan for fixing padding (if user wants):
1. **Per-edge padding into own-size hug**: change the wrapper QML so implicit size accounts for per-edge margins. E.g., add `plPadTop/plPadRight/plPadBottom/plPadLeft` properties and compute implicitWidth = lay.implicitWidth + plPadLeft + plPadRight; implicitHeight = lay.implicitHeight + plPadTop + plPadBottom. And applyPadding sets the corresponding `plPad*` AND `anchors.*Margin`. For uniform, set all four (or plPad = value and the four plPad* from plPad). This makes hug sizing correct for per-edge.

2. **Padding on non-stack views**: implement a generic padding (e.g., a wrapper/padding box or adjust content margins). This is more involved — Qt items don't have padding. Options:
   - For a leaf like Text, wrap it in an Item with padding (but that changes the node's widget identity/hit-testing).
   - Use `contentItem` margins? Not general.
   - Simplest spec-faithful: apply padding to a Text via its own `leftPadding/topPadding/rightPadding/bottomPadding`? QQuickText doesn't have padding. QQuickControls TextField/Label do (`TextField` has `leftPadding` etc. via Control). For a plain Text, no padding.
   - This is a larger feature. Given scope, I'd recommend: document non-stack padding as a gap (like other renderers), OR implement a generic padding via a background/padding wrapper.

Given the demo only uses padding on stacks (VStack/HStack) and composite controls, the critical fix is #1 (per-edge hug). Non-stack padding (#2) is a spec gap not exercised by the demo.

Let me be concise but complete.

## Answer: yes — but only partially, and per-edge padding has a real bug

### What's implemented (`qt_layer.cpp`)
- `PADDING` (uniform) + `PADDING_TOP/RIGHT/BOTTOM/LEFT` (per-edge) + `CONTENT_MARGINS` all map to `applyPadding` (`:1774-1787`).
- On a **stack** (VStack/HStack/lazy/proxy/composite) the wrapper QML carries `plPad`, which drives both the inner layout's `anchors.margins` and the wrapper's **implicit size** (`:405-455`). Uniform padding sets `plPad` + `anchors.margins`; per-edge sets `anchors.topMargin`/etc.
- Tested by `padding_insets_the_stack_content` (uniform margins + one per-edge `topMargin`).

### What's broken / missing (spec deviations)

1. **Per-edge padding is not reflected in the stack's own-size hug.** The implicit-size binding is `implicitWidth: lay.implicitWidth + 2 * plPad` — it only reads the **uniform** `plPad`. Per-edge `topMargin/rightMargin/…` inset the layout but leave `plPad = 0`, so a hug stack (e.g. the demo's `subtitlePill` with `padding(edges(6,12,6,12))`, and the dividers with `padding(edges(0,0,0,10))`) sizes to its **unpadded** content and the inset content overflows the box (its `Rectangle` background is `anchors.fill: parent`, so the padding is visually lost).

2. **Padding is a no-op on non-stack views.** `applyPadding` early-returns when `layoutOf(item)` is null (`:1676-1678`). Spec (MODIFIERS.md:17) says ".padding works on a Text and a VStack alike" — so `.padding` on a `Text`/`Image`/`Button` (non-composite) is silently dropped.

3. **Uniform-vs-per-edge precedence for sizing.** Per-edge correctly overrides `anchors.margins` visually, but `plPad` still holds the old uniform value, so the implicit size is wrong after an edge override.

### Proposed fix plan

**Phase 1 (demo-critical) — make per-edge padding participate in hug sizing.**
- Add four `plPadTop/Right/Bottom/Left` properties to the stack wrapper QML; compute `implicitWidth = lay.implicitWidth + plPadLeft + plPadRight`, `implicitHeight = lay.implicitHeight + plPadTop + plPadBottom`.
- `applyPadding`: uniform sets all four `plPad*` + `anchors.margins`; per-edge sets the matching `plPad*` + `anchors.*Margin` (so per-edge wins on both inset and size).

In the diff, inserts happen before props (per renderer.rs). But the padding could be applied to a node that is re-parented later. For robust behavior, I should also call `applyPaddingEdges(id)` at the end of insertChild (after the child is attached) for nodes with pad_state. Let me add that: in insertChild, after `child->setParentItem(attach)` and the fill handling, call `if (g.pad_state.count(childId)) applyPaddingEdges(childId);`. But for re-parenting (diff moves a node), the padding should be re-applied. Let me add a call in insertChild for safety.

Actually, the diff's `children_diff` may RE-INSERT a node when order changes (remove_child + insert_child), and pad_state persists. The re-insert would attach to a possibly different parent. So re-applying padding on insert is good. Let me add after the fill handling in insertChild:

parts.text:
Existing tests still pass. Now add the new tests:

1. `stack_hugs_including_per_edge_padding` — per-edge padding affects hug implicit size + child position.
2. `leaf_padding_insets_a_root_view` — a root Text with PADDING → anchors margins → size/position inset.
3. `leaf_padding_insets_within_a_stack` — a Text inside an HStack with padding → Layout margins → position offset.

Let me design them carefully.

**Test 1: per-edge hug**
```
create ZSTACK 1; insert CONTENT 1
create VSTACK 2; insert 1 2
set PADDING_LEFT 2 = 12; PADDING_RIGHT=8; PADDING_TOP=6; PADDING_BOTTOM=4
create TEXT 3; insert 2 3; set WIDTH 3 100; set HEIGHT 3 40
apply; render_once
assert implicit_size(2,0) = 100 + 12 + 8 = 120
assert implicit_size(2,1) = 40 + 6 + 4 = 50
```
Also assert the child is inset: position(3,0) = 12 (left margin), position(3,1) = 6 (top margin). Wait — the child is inside the ColumnLayout; the layout has anchors margins top=6,left=12,... so the layout is inset within the wrapper. But the child's x/y relative to the layout = 0 (the layout positions at 0,0 within its inset area). So `widget_position(3)` returns child->x() relative to the layout = 0, not 12. Hmm. The padding inset is on the layout's position within the wrapper, not the child within the layout. So position(3) = 0. To assert the inset, I'd need the layout's position relative to the wrapper. There's no direct hook. The existing `padding_insets_the_stack_content` checks the layout's anchors margins via the padding hook. So for test 1, rely on implicit size (the key Phase 1 fix) + the padding hook.

Actually, I can assert the child's *absolute* position? There's no hook. Let me just assert the implicit size (the bug fix) and the padding hook values.

Let me use the existing `pathland_qt_layer_padding(2, "topMargin") == 6`, `"leftMargin"==12`, etc., plus implicit sizes.

**Test 2: leaf root padding**
```
create TEXT 1; insert CONTENT 1; set_text "padded"
set PADDING 1 = 10
apply; render_once
assert position(1,0) ~ 10, position(1,1) ~ 10
assert size(1,0) ~ 400, size(1,1) ~ 200
```
Root Text is anchored.fill g.root (420x220). anchors margins 10 → inset → x=10,y=10,w=400,h=200. Good.

But wait: does `applyPaddingEdges` for the leaf root set anchors.topMargin? parent = g.root (not a layout) → sets anchors.*Margin. And the Text has anchors.fill set (insertChild parentId==0). So anchors margins apply. Good.

But careful: the property is applied after insert (props after inserts), so the anchors.fill exists. Good.

Also the Text's implicit size vs anchored size: anchors.fill forces size 400x200. Good.

**Test 3: leaf in a stack**
```
create HSTACK 1; insert CONTENT 1; set WIDTH 1 = 300; set HEIGHT 1 = 100
create TEXT 2; insert 1 2; set WIDTH 2 50; set HEIGHT 2 20
set PADDING_TOP 2 = 6; PADDING_LEFT 2 = 12
apply; render_once
assert position(2,0) ~ 12, position(2,1) ~ 6  (Layout margins)
assert size(2) ~ 50x20 (own size unchanged)
```
Hmm — the Text is inside the HStack's RowLayout. Layout.leftMargin=12, topMargin=6. The item's x within the layout = 12 (leftMargin), y = 6 (topMargin). Its width stays 50 (preferred). Good.

But the HStack is a root → anchored.fill → 420x220, ignoring the fixed 300x100? If the HStack is a root (parent 0), insertChild sets anchors.fill → overrides fixed size. So the fixed W/H is ignored. To control the stack size, put the HStack inside a ZStack (like the other tests). Let me do:
```
create ZSTACK 1; insert CONTENT 1
create HSTACK 2; insert 1 2; set WIDTH 2 300; set HEIGHT 2 100
create TEXT 3; insert 2 3; set WIDTH 3 50; set HEIGHT 3 20
set PADDING_TOP 3 = 6; PADDING_LEFT 3 = 12
apply; render_once
assert position(3,0) ~ 12, position(3,1) ~ 6
```

### ScrollView — `SCROLLVIEW` 0x14

A scrollable content container. **Layout-greedy on both axes** by default — it
fills the available space (SwiftUI `ScrollView` / Compose scroll semantics); an
explicit `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` overrides it (LAYOUT.md §layout-greedy primitives).
**Properties**: layout modifiers (Fixed/Fill frames, `PADDING`/`CONTENT_MARGINS`
as an inset).

**Content.** The **first child** is the content; a scroll view carries a single
content subtree (typically a stack), matching SwiftUI/Compose's single-content
contract. The content is measured with an **unbounded proposal** on both axes —
it may grow beyond the viewport (that is what scrolls). The **viewport** is the
scroll view's allocated box; a Hug `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` — or a Hug parent proposal
on an axis — sizes the viewport to the content's natural size on that axis (the
viewport fits the content, so that axis does not scroll).

**Overflow.** A scroll view scrolls its content rather than clipping it — the
viewport clips by virtue of scrolling; `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS` on the scroll view has
no further effect on the content.

**Events.** With the `SCROLL` listener bit (bit 8) the renderer reports the
content offset in logical points via `EVENT::SCROLL`; with `WHEEL` (bit 9) it
reports wheel/trackpad deltas via `EVENT::WHEEL` (both draft — see
[EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md)).

### LazyVGrid — `LAZY_VGRID` 0x15

Virtualized vertical grid. **Allocation is identical to `GRID`** — row-major
cells, `GRID_COLUMNS` = column count (Fixed pins it, `FILL`/absent = auto-fit),
equal `1fr` columns, uniform `SPACING` gap, per-cell alignment, hug-to-content
own size. The only difference is **realization**: a renderer MAY defer realizing
off-screen cells until scrolled into view and MAY discard realized cells that
leave the viewport. Realization never changes layout — a cell's position is
always its row-major index in the full cell list. Typically nested inside a
`SCROLLVIEW`.

### LazyHGrid — `LAZY_HGRID` 0x16

### Implementation facts (verified)

- Content child attaches to the ScrollView's `contentItem` (`insertChild:2385`); the renderer never resizes it → content keeps its own size (unbounded), matching the spec.
- **Deviation**: `HUG_CONTENT` (`-2`) maps to `PL_SIZE_NONE`, so `greedyFills` still makes a SCROLLVIEW fill — `WIDTH/HEIGHT = HUG_CONTENT` is ignored (spec says an explicit size overrides greed, and a Hug axis sizes the viewport to content).

1. **`scroll_view_fills_by_default`** (stretch)
   - SCROLLVIEW (no frame) as a child of a fixed-size VStack → `widget_fill(0/1)==1` and `widget_size == stack size`.

 Design-token contract: `spec/TOKENS.md`.
 
 **Language split.** The crate is a **hybrid**:
 - **Rust** owns the shared decode core (`pathland-render-core`), a sent-state
   **delta diff** that turns each frame into a batch of C-compatible commands,
   the `Pump` transport seam (frames in / events out), the Qt main-loop shell,
   and the C ABI for foreign hosts.
 - **C++** (in `src/qt/`) owns the Qt application shell (QGuiApplication +
   QQuickWindow + QQmlEngine + a QML-facing `Bridge` QObject) and applies the
   delta command batch to QML items. Built via `cc` + `moc` in `build.rs`;
   needs Qt6 dev libs (Homebrew: `qtbase qtdeclarative qtmultimedia`).
 
 ## Implemented

   Linux CI), runs `moc` on the bridge, compiles the C++ layer with `cc`, and
   links the Qt frameworks/dylibs (framework search via the transitive

   Rc<RefCell<RingTransport>>, on_event)` mirrors `pathland_render_gtk::run`;
   the pump borrow is held across frame application (zero-copy batch view of the
   shared ring).
 
 - **Navigation adapter (spec DSL.md §4.5)**: a VSTACK/HSTACK slot carrying the
   `ROUTE` property promotes to the renderer's nav container and reconciles a
   page stack **by depth** (`NAV_DEPTH`): pop down to the app's depth, then
   `Refresh` (same route), `Push` (deeper + new route), or `Replace` (same
   depth, new route) — mirroring the GTK `AdwNavigationView` adapter. `PlatformDefault`
   chrome wraps each page in a header with a native back button (`→`
   `navigateBack` → `Event::Navigate { url: None }`); `NAV_CHROME=1` (`Custom`)
   pushes the bare destination. The back-stack stays app-owned; the page stack
   is the renderer's rendered-output cache. **Implementation note:** Qt Quick
   has no native navigation container and `StackView`'s `push`/`pop` are
   QML-callable-only (not invokable from C++ via `QMetaObject`), so the nav
   container is a plain `Item` whose pages the renderer manages (only the top
   visible) — a renderer-owned page cache, same statelessness contract.
   **Page sizing:** each page wrapper is anchored to fill the nav container
   (`placeDestination`), so the header/content/destination chain is sized and the
   destination subtree fills the content area (previously the page wrapper was
   attached unsized, collapsing the content to 0×0 and showing only an
   overflowing title).
 
 - **Post-merge protocol parity (October 2026)**: the crate was merged onto the
   shared `PARAMETER` rename and now maps the protocol surface added on `main`:
   - `ICON` (0x0B) → a `Text` item whose glyph is resolved from `ICON_NAME` by a
     renderer-owned canonical-name map (unknown names fall back to a dot), with
     `COLOR`/`FONT_SIZE` reuse (spec/ICONS.md).
   - `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` (0x30) → **non-visual** (layout-transparent: created but
     never attached) hosting a QML `MediaPlayer` + `AudioOutput`
     (spec/MEDIA.md).
   - `VIDEO` (0x0A) → a `VideoOutput` surface; `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID` binds its
     `source` to the referenced controller's `MediaPlayer` (a reference, not a
     parent/child edge).
   - `PROXY_VIEW` (0x1E) → a transparent vertical container.
   - `SIZE_THAT_FITS` (0x17) → a greedy two-axis slot; its one selected child
     fills it.
   - `GRID_ROW` (0x1D) → a row-grouping container whose cells flatten into
     the parent Grid.
 - **Shared decode parity** (`pathland-render-core`): `LIST`-typed properties
   (`FIT_QUERY`) decode into `HostNode::lists`, and `PARAMETER::SET_DATE` into
   `HostNode::date` — so the Qt layer can measure fit slots and format dates.
 - **`SIZE_THAT_FITS` fit measurement**: the slot's `FIT_QUERY` thresholds reach
   the C++ layer as CSV; a width change derives the fit index (largest
   `minWidth` ≤ allocated width; equal thresholds keep the lower index; empty
   table → 0) and reports `FIT_CHANGED` once after the first measure, then only
   when the index changes. The report is a layout result, not a value echo, so
   it is not suppressed while a frame's properties are applied. The slot shows
   exactly one selected child, which fills the slot.
 - **`GRID_ROW` flattening**: a row's cells attach directly to the parent Grid
   (row-major), so columns align across rows; the row item takes no cell.
 - **`DATE_PICKER`**: `SET_DATE` (days since epoch + millis of day) renders as an
   ISO date (with time when nonzero) in a QML text field — a QML approximation
   (Qt Quick has no native date picker).
 - **Events** (spec/EVENTS.md): pointer `hover`/`leave` (`POINTER_MOVE`
   hovering/leaving) from the listener `MouseArea`; `KEY_DOWN`/`KEY_UP` for the
   focused text input (component-type/key-listener gated); `FOCUS_CHANGED` /
   `EDITING_CHANGED` / `SUBMIT` for text inputs (gated by the matching
   `EVENT_LISTENERS` bits); BackSpace is native back unless a text input is
   focused (focus-aware, no longer deferred).
 - **Visual styling layer** (parity with the web/GTK demos):
   - `BACKGROUND_COLOR` / `BORDER_*` / `BORDER_RADIUS` render on a background
     `Rectangle` behind a container's content (stacks reuse an injected
     `pl<id>bg`; plain containers create one lazily); `Rectangle`-backed nodes
     set them directly. `RESET_NODE` clears them.
   - **Composite control mode** (spec/PRIMITIVES.md §2): a `Button` that gains
     children is promoted from the native widget to a bare `Item`+`ColumnLayout`
     shell that renders the app's `ButtonStyle` body, so `PlainButtonStyle` /
     `BorderedButtonStyle` buttons look like the web/GTK ones. Leaf buttons stay
     native.
   - **Foreground inheritance** (CSS `color`): a container's `COLOR` is inherited
     by descendant `Text`/`Icon` that don't set their own.
   - **Layout defaults (spec/LAYOUT.md)**: the cross axis **hugs** by default
     (never CSS `align-items:stretch`); only an *effectively FILL* child stretches
     — explicit `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT=FILL`, a layout-greedy primitive (`SPACER` main,
     `DIVIDER` cross, `COLOR`/`SCROLLVIEW`/`SIZE_THAT_FITS` both), or **fill
     propagation** (a Hug stack/ZStack/proxy whose subtree carries a FILL
-    child/greedy filler). `ALIGNMENT` only positions (`Fill(3)` = default hug).
+    child/greedy filler). An explicit fixed size **or `HUG_CONTENT`**
+    (`PL_SIZE_HUG`) overrides a primitive's natural greed. `ALIGNMENT` only
+    positions (`Fill(3)` = default hug).
     Recomputed at each frame boundary (`recomputeLayout`), so `RESET_NODE`'s
     style reset can't wipe it. Plus `CONTENT_MARGINS`.
   - **`TEXT_STYLE`** applies a base typography (size + weight) that raw
     `FONT_SIZE`/`FONT_WEIGHT` override; **`SHADOW_*`** draws a best-effort
     offset shadow layer.
 - **Media transport** (spec/MEDIA.md): `MEDIA_SOURCE`, `PLAYBACK_STATE`
   (play/pause), `MEDIA_POSITION` (seek, seconds→ms), `MEDIA_VOLUME` /
   `MEDIA_MUTED` (via `AudioOutput`), `MEDIA_LOOP`, `MEDIA_RATE`, and the
   `MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED` / `MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED` / `MEDIA_ENDED` /
   `MEDIA_VOLUME_CHANGED` / `MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED` reports (reported by the
   controller's component type, not gated by `BINDING_ID`; programmatic sets are
   echo-suppressed). A play/pause declared before the source is re-applied when
   the source lands.
 - **Layout/property parity**: `OFFSET_X/Y`, `POSITION_X/Y`, `MIN/IDEAL/MAX_*`,
   `CONTENT_MODE` (image fit/fill), `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`, `BORDER_COLOR` /
   `BORDER_WIDTH` / `BORDER_RADIUS`, `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`, `LINE_LIMIT`,
   `TRUNCATION_MODE`, and `GRID_COLUMNS` (via the `Layout` attached properties
   where applicable).
 - **Headless test hang fixed**: Qt adds the executable's directory to QML's
   implicit import path; a `cargo test` binary lives in a huge `target/debug/deps`
   and plugin resolution scanned it for minutes. The shell now drops the
   application directory from the engine's import path at init, so
   `cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` completes in ~2s (no copy-to-temp workaround).
 
 ## Not implemented / gaps
 
 - **`MENU` popup item list**: Qt 6 has no `MenuButton`; the trigger is a
   `Button` and the action-item popup is not built (documented gap).
 - **`COLOR_PICKER`** remains a `Button` approximation (a QML color-swatch popup
   is a follow-up); `DATE_PICKER` is an ISO-text QML approximation, not a native
   dialog.
 - **`PICKER` option styling** and `SHAPE` path approximation. Native **leaf**
   controls keep Qt Quick Controls' own chrome (background/border); the styling
   layer covers containers, composite controls, and `Rectangle`-backed nodes.
 - **Icons** are renderer-owned glyphs (the canonical `ICON_NAME` → a Unicode
   symbol), not the web's SVG/Lucide set — recognizable but not pixel-identical.
 - **Shadows** are an offset rectangle approximation, not a blurred
   `MultiEffect` shadow.
 - **Keys/events beyond the focused text input**: keys are reported for a focused
   text input; keys on other focused controls, `SCROLL`/`WHEEL`, and

   `anchors.fill` on its children, so a `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` `FILL` inside a Grid

   does), so the demo marks the slider bound via a `BINDING_ID` on the retained
   tree; a real `.value(Signal)` DSL binding is a DSL/engine feature.

   the renderer consumes ROUTE/NAV_DEPTH (exercised by the nav adapter tests).

   intermediate pages (same gaps as the GTK renderer).

   `MusicPlayerView` (app-driven media) via `pathland_qt_run_ring`.

Done — **83 tests pass** (`cargo test -p pathland-render-qt`).

### Renderer changes (spec compliance)
- **`HUG_CONTENT` (`-2`) now overrides layout greed.** Added `PL_SIZE_HUG`; `applySize` maps `-2` → HUG; `effectiveFill` returns `false` for `PL_SIZE_HUG` (like `FIXED`, it bounds the subtree). - **`reconcileScrollSize`**: a HUG axis on a `SCROLLVIEW` sets its `implicitWidth/Height` from the content's natural size (Qt's `ScrollView` has no implicit size), so the viewport hugs the content.
- **`insertChild` greedy-anchor guard**: a greedy primitive's automatic `anchors.fill` is skipped when an explicit `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` (FIXED/FILL/HUG) is present, so explicit sizing wins.

### The chain of components/modifiers involved

1. **`SCROLLVIEW` (0x14)** — the primary culprit. In the Qt renderer its content child is attached to the ScrollView's `contentItem` (`insertChild` ~:2385) but **never sized to the viewport**. Per the "unbounded content" model, a hug content stays hug.

3. **`TrackRowView` → `Button` with `frame(width FILL)`** — the row explicitly fills, but `FILL` is *relative to the content VStack's width*, which is collapsed. The author even wrote a comment expecting full-width rows.
4. **`Spacer`** (inside each row's `HStack`, plus the trailing `Spacer` in the content VStack) — greedy, but bounded by the collapsed width.
5. `LibraryView`'s own `frame(width FILL, height FILL)` is **fine** (it fills the `ZStack`); the collapse is *inside* the `ScrollView`.

### Root cause (renderer)
Fill propagation works within a stack/`ZStack` because `recomputeLayout` calls `applyChildAxes`/`applyZStackAlignment` against a **sized** container. But a ScrollView's `contentItem` is a plain `Flickable` content — nothing sizes the content to the viewport, so:

`contentVStack` (hug) ← rows `WIDTH=FILL` fill **its** width (≈0) → rows collapse.

The content VStack is "effectively FILL" horizontally (its `Button` rows carry `WIDTH=FILL`) and vertically (the trailing `Spacer`), but that fill has no viewport to materialize against.

Extend the ScrollView reconcile (`reconcileScrollSize`, `qt_layer.cpp` ~:1225, already wired into `recomputeLayout`):

- For a `SCROLLVIEW` with a content child, on each axis where `effectiveFill(content, axis, /*main=*/false)` is **true**, size the content against the viewport:
  - horizontal → `content.setWidth(scroll.width())`

- Re-derive on ScrollView resize (connect `widthChanged`/`heightChanged`, same pattern as `ZStack`).

This makes the FILL rows propagate up through the content VStack and materialize against the viewport, expanding the library horizontally.

### Cross axis

- A **Fixed** or **Hug** child keeps its own size on the cross axis and is
  **positioned** by the container's `ALIGNMENT`.
- **`ALIGNMENT` positions but never resizes.** It selects the placement of
  Fixed/Hug children within leftover space; it does not stretch them. The value
  is a **2D position code** (the [ZStack table](./PRIMITIVES.md#zstack--zstack-0x12)):
  a stack reads a single axis (a `VStack` the horizontal component, an `HStack`
  the vertical — codes `0/1/2`), a `ZStack`/grid both axes. With no `ALIGNMENT`
  (code `0`/absent) the default cross-axis position is the **start**. Code `3`
  is `top-center`, never a stretch; stretching lives in the **child's size
  kind** (`WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` = `FILL`).
- Only a **`Fill`-sized child** fills the container's cross size.
- **The default is *hug*, not stretch.** A child with no cross-axis size is NOT
  stretched to fill the cross axis. This deliberately matches **SwiftUI**
  (children report their ideal size; a `VStack`/`HStack` aligns them) and
  **Compose** (Row/Column children wrap content cross-axis unless
  `fillMaxWidth/Height`), rather than CSS flexbox's `align-items: stretch`
  default. A renderer must therefore NOT stretch cross-axis children implicitly
  (e.g. the web renderer uses `align-items: flex-start`, not the flex default).

### Layout-greedy primitives

The cross-axis hug default has **four intrinsic exceptions** — primitives whose
native behavior is to fill space (SwiftUI/Compose precedent), so an app does not
need an explicit `FILL` frame to get their natural behavior:

| Primitive | Greedy on | Precedent |
|-----------|-----------|-----------|

These rules are the bugs-fixed-and-avoided model of the reference renderers:

Content-bearing views fit their content **inside** their allocated box:

SwiftUI's `ScrollView` is **not** greedy on both axes: it only expands on its **scroll axis**; on the cross axis it **shrinks to fit content** unless the content is told to fill (`.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)`). The current spec ("layout-greedy on **both** axes") is wrong, and it's reflected in the shared `greedyFills` model (GTK `layout.rs:93` and Qt both treat `SCROLLVIEW` as both-axes greedy).

## Correct model (to encode in the spec)

| Axis | ScrollView's own size | Content proposal |
|------|----------------------|------------------|
| **Scroll axis** (vertical) | greedy — fills available space | **unbounded** — grows past the viewport (= scrolls) |
| **Cross axis** (horizontal) | **hugs content** by default (shrinks to fit); fill **propagates** — a `FILL`-width content child makes the viewport `FILL`-width | **bounded** to the viewport's cross size |

So full-width scroll content = a `FILL`-width child of the content stack (`.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)`), never by stretching the content or the viewport itself.

   `RingOpcodeSink`. **`Signals.constant` / `ConstantSignal`**: a view or
   modifier holds one `Signal<T>` per reactive value (the raw `of(T)` overload is
   sugar for a constant); the emitter treats a constant as a plain, non-reactive
   property (no binding/effect).
 - **Structural reactivity** (spec DSL.md §3.4): `Conditional.when(Signal<Boolean>,
   then, else)` and `when(Signal<T>, Case.of(...)...) / Case.otherwise(...)` —
   statically importable lowercase factories on a final class (mirrors
   `Signals`; `if`/`switch`/`case`/`else` are Java keywords). A structural
   container materializes as a `Group` slot (bare `VSTACK` node); the emitter's
   structural effect reconciles the slot's single child on selector change —
   position+type-stable ids, `TREE` deltas only, identical recompute emits
   **zero** opcodes, nested containers work, and the slot's subtree owns its own
   bindings. `RenderResult` routing maps are now live unmodifiable views (a swap
   updates tap/text/value/date routing after mount).
 - **Router** (`dev.pathland.view.router`, spec DSL.md §4.5): `Route` (absolute
   path, `pathOnly()` strips query/fragment), `RouteTable` (literal + `:param`
   patterns, guards → `replace()` redirect, `fallback` 404), `Router`
   (`Signal<Route>` + back-stack; `navigate`/`push`/`pop`/`replace`/`back`,
   `handlePlatformNavigation`/`handleEvent`), **`Navigation`** (the ergonomic
   facade: `Navigation.navigator(initialPath).route(...).fallback(...).build()`
   collapses table + router + seeding, `Navigation.container(router)` is the slot,
   `Navigation.isActive(router, path)` → a reactive `Signal<Boolean>` for
   active-route styling, `Navigation.ROUTER` = the `EnvironmentKey<Router>`),
   **`Params`** (typed path-param access — `get`/
   `intValue`/`longValue`/`doubleValue`/`booleanValue`/`path` — replacing the raw
   `Map` in `RouteHandler`), **a bound router** (`Navigation.navigator()...
   .build(WritableSignal<String>)` — the router binds to the host-provided
   `Platform.ACTIVE_PATH` signal: external writes are re-routed **guard-aware**,
   its own navigation is mirrored back, the initial value is guard-processed), and
   **generic scoped environment values**
   (`EnvironmentKey`/`EnvironmentValues` + the `EnvironmentBinding` modifier value
   (`environmentBinding(e -> e.key(key).value(value))`) +
   `Environment.value(key)` — the `.environment` style, hierarchical nearest-
   wins; a `NavigationContainer` scopes `Navigation.ROUTER` to its destination
   subtree and structural slots re-apply the incoming scope on re-render via
   `PathlandNode.environmentForChildren`/`Emitter.reconcileSlot`; **reads always
   return a signal** — `Environment.value(key)` → `Signal<T>`, a value injected as
   a `Signal` comes back as the same instance (bindable for reactive updates) and a
   plain value is wrapped in a constant signal; a read made before the key is bound
   returns a **lazy signal** that captures the binding on the first `.get()` during
   render, enabling the `@Environment` **field style**
   (`private final Signal<Router> router = Environment.value(Navigation.ROUTER);`)),
   plus the
   **universal active platform path** (`Platform.ACTIVE_PATH` =
   `EnvironmentKey<String>`, the host injects a writable signal — provided for every
   app with or without navigation — read via `Environment.value` and observed via
   the `PathChange` modifier value (`pathChange(p -> p.listener(...))`) /
   reading the signal; fires on every change incl.
   the initial value),
   `NavigationContainer` (structural
   slot emitting the `ROUTE` property coalesced into the same frame as the
   destination swap, plus a `NAV_DEPTH` U32 back-stack-depth property
   (`router.depth()` = stack size + 1; `push`+1 / `pop`−1 / `replace` unchanged)
   so native navigation adapters reconcile their page stack by depth, a
   `NAV_CHROME` chrome-mode property (`Chrome.PLATFORM_DEFAULT` / `Chrome.CUSTOM`
   — the renderer supplies default navigation chrome, or the developer owns all
   nav UI), and a `TRANSITION` PlatformDefault hint renderers may use
   to animate the swap), `NavigationLink` (a `BUTTON` that pushes — both
   explicit-router and **router-agnostic** overloads). **Any component can change
   the route** (spec DSL.md §4.5): `Button.make(b -> …).modifiers(NavigationIntent.navigate/push/replace(path))`
   (`NavigationIntent`) and router-agnostic
   `NavigationLink.make(l -> l.label("..").to(path))` record a
   `NavOp` intent on the node; the emitter resolves it to the **nearest
   enclosing** `Router` (the `NavigationContainer` the component lives under)
   during the retained-tree walk and exposes it on
   `RenderResult.navigateActions` (a live `node id → Runnable` map like
   `tapActions`), which the host routes on tap before `tapActions`. The route is a
   **plain signal** (not persisted; the URL is the web's persistence layer) and
   the host **seeds it before mount** via `navigate(...)` — no `Location`, no
   environment-carried route. A `NAVIGATE` event (`Event.navigate(url)` /
   `Event.navigateBack()`, wire round-trip via `FrameCodec`) routes into the
   router through `RenderResult.navigateHandler`.
 - **Wire codec** (`transport`): `FrameCodec` — self-contained `PLPL` frames
   both directions, `encodeEvents`/`decodeEvents` (host→guest events with
   `TEXT_CHANGED` string-section offsets), and **`META::ENVIRONMENT`**
   (`isEnvironment`/`decodeEnvironment` → `EnvironmentData` — the platform
   environment: viewport + initial route; SSR synthesizes it from the request,
   the DOM client sends/enriches it over the WebSocket).
 - **JNA ring interop** (`ffm`): lazy `libpathland_core` binding, zero JNI;
   `PathlandCore.ringMut(handle)` borrows the underlying ring for the in-process
   GTK renderer (`pathland_gtk_run_ring`), and `RingOpcodeSink` is the zero-copy
   guest writer.
 - **Input dispatch** (`emit.InputDispatcher`): routes raw `EVENT`s into the
   `RenderResult` registries (tap / navigate / text / value / date, `NAVIGATE`
   URL → active path, back → router). Shared by the server session
   (`PathlandSession.dispatch`) and the native GTK host, so both route events
   identically and neither reaches into view internals.
 - **`BINDING_ID` on the ring path**: for a `RingOpcodeSink`, the emitter sets
   `BINDING_ID` (= the node's id) on every text/value/date-bound control so the
   GTK renderer's transport-aware event guard fires (`TEXT_CHANGED` /
   `VALUE_CHANGED`). The frame (SSR) path never emits it, keeping server output
   unchanged.
 - **State** (`state`): `StateStore`/`PersistentState`/`State`, auto-wired by
   `pathland-view-processor`.
 - **Design tokens**: `Color` is `(argb, token)` — `Color.token("color.primary")`
   (incl. `dark.*` paths) usable in every color-taking modifier
   (`ForegroundStyle`/`Background`/`Border`/`Tint`, and the `Color` view). The
   emitter sends token refs as the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type (path in the frame's
   string section / arena) in both `FrameOpcodeSink` and `RingOpcodeSink`
   (spec/TOKENS.md).
 - **`Theme` / `AdaptiveTheme` (global overrides)**: `Theme` — single-value
   builders (`color`/`f32`/`u32`/`u8`/`string`) for one scheme; `AdaptiveTheme(light,
   dark)` composes a light + dark pair. Both implement the `ThemeData` interface
   (`emit`/`emitInto`); `Theme.emit`/`AdaptiveTheme.emit` write one frame of
   `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides (the dark theme's with the `dark.` prefix),
   and `OpcodeSink.setDesignToken` puts path + STRING values into the string
   section (frame) / arena (ring). The `Emitter` takes a `ThemeData` and rides it
   into the mount + resync frames. Overrides are renderer-global — they never
   re-emit nodes.
 
 ## Not implemented / gaps
 
 - `ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID` are usable as modifiers (`actionId`/`bindingId`); the
   Java model routes events by node id through the emitter's registries
   (`RenderResult`), so the frame (SSR) path does not set them automatically.
   On the ring (desktop) path the emitter auto-sets `BINDING_ID` for bound
   controls (see Implemented) — the GTK renderer gates value/text events on it.
 - Structural reconcile does not emit `SET_PROPERTY` for a *removed* property on
   a matched node (the wire has no unset; the renderer keeps the last value) —
   consistent with the Rust engine.
 
 ## Verified by
 
 `mvn test` (JDK 17+) — emitter, codec round-trips (incl. `NAVIGATE`), signals,
 state, structural-reactivity (`ConditionalTest`) and the router (`RouterTest`:
 initial route + `ROUTE` property + `NAV_DEPTH` depth tracking + `NAV_CHROME`
 chrome mode, destination swap deltas, back-stack, params, guard redirect,
 fallback, `NAVIGATE` routing, `NavigationLink`, the **declarative nav
 intents** (`.navigate/.push/.replace` + router-agnostic `NavigationLink`
 resolving to the nearest enclosing router via `navigateActions`), the
 **`Navigation` facade / `Params` / `isActive`**, the **scoped environment
 values** (`View.environment` + `Environment.value` hierarchy/restore), and the
 **universal active path** (a bound router re-routing guard-aware on external
 signal writes + mirroring its own navigation; `onPathChange` firing on changes));
 the JNA ring
 test runs when `libpathland_core` is on `java.library.path`. The v2 authoring
 surface is covered by `ViewBuilderTest` (with/modifiers/children any-order) and
 `ModifierWithTest` (modifier `with(...)`, enum/`Font` value-is-modifier,
 `Frame.with` builder); signals-first configs by `ReactiveConfigTest` (a
 non-constant value member re-emits exactly one `SET_PROPERTY` — boolean, float,
 enum, string, container spacing — and a constant registers no binding). CI proves
 every LTS from 17 (Temurin 17/21/25).

 **Last updated:** October 15, 2026

   the read cursor numerically (the producer wraps through 0), and the naive
   `write < read` guard in `read_events` / `Host::frames` **permanently
   deadlocked the ring** at the wrap boundary — the reader never advanced again,
   the writer sat "full", and every subsequent drain returned empty (the GTK
   demo's "UI freezes some time into a song, audio keeps playing": events were
   written but `drain_events` returned 0 forever). Both readers now count the
   pending run modulo the ring size and drain across the wrap in ring order
   (`Host::frames` drains the wrapped head in one call and the tail in the next,
   preserving opcode order). Event drains also take a `max` bound
   (`drain_event_opcodes_max`) so a fixed-size C buffer never drops events it
   could not copy. Regression tests: `ring::tests::read_events_drains_a_wrapped_producer`

   codec over the shared ring** (event-arena absolute offset for a `ROUTE`
   field) and a native emitter are not wired yet — the web path encodes/decodes
   it in the TS client + Java `FrameCodec` (batch string section).

   no named value constants. (`ROLE` and `TEXT_STYLE` are now the canonical
   exceptions — see `constants::role` / `constants::text_style` above; the
   remaining enum codes live in the specs + the `pathland-ts-codegen` enum

   stores numeric properties + design-token refs only). `ROUTE` (STRING) will
   need a small string-property capability when the Rust router lands (Phase 3);
